definition: AWS High Availability Design is a core concept in AWS Developer Associate. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What AWS High Availability Design is
theory.body: AWS High Availability Design describes the methods and patterns used within AWS Developer Associate to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: AWS High Availability Design is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why AWS High Availability Design matters
theory.body: Without AWS High Availability Design, systems built with AWS Developer Associate are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How AWS High Availability Design works
theory.body: The mechanism behind AWS High Availability Design follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of AWS High Availability Design.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of AWS High Availability Design
theory.body: AWS High Availability Design offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
